title: Weighted Power Mean Inequality Chain
description: The weighted power mean M_p^w(a,b) = (w₁aᵖ + w₂bᵖ)^{1/p} satisfies wHM ≤ wGM ≤ wAM ≤ wQM for weights w₁+w₂=1. Mathlib's Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted directly proves wGM ≤ wAM; the chain is completed by Jensen for x² and a reciprocal argument for wHM ≤ wGM.

overview.historicalContext: The power mean inequality chain min ≤ HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM ≤ max was proved in the parent entry for equal weights (1/2, 1/2). Robertson (1929) and others studied the weighted generalizations in the context of operator theory and quantum mechanics. The weighted AM-GM is a cornerstone of convex analysis, following from Jensen's inequality applied to the logarithm.
overview.problemStatement: For weights w₁, w₂ ≥ 0 with w₁ + w₂ = 1 and positive reals a, b, prove the weighted mean chain: wHM(w₁,w₂,a,b) ≤ wGM(w₁,w₂,a,b) ≤ wAM(w₁,w₂,a,b) ≤ wQM(w₁,w₂,a,b). Confirm that Mathlib has the infrastructure to formalize this generalization.
overview.text: The open question asks whether Mathlib contains the infrastructure to formalize the weighted power mean monotonicity. The answer is YES: Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted directly proves wGM ≤ wAM, Jensen for x² (purely algebraic, using w₁w₂(a-b)² ≥ 0) proves wAM ≤ wQM, and wHM ≤ wGM follows by applying wGM ≤ wAM to the reciprocals a⁻¹ and b⁻¹ via Real.inv_rpow.
overview.proofStrategy: Three steps: (1) wGM ≤ wAM: direct application of Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted. (2) wAM ≤ wQM: square both sides, reduce to w₁w₂(a-b)² ≥ 0 via nlinarith. (3) wHM ≤ wGM: apply wGM ≤ wAM to a⁻¹ and b⁻¹; use Real.inv_rpow to simplify (a⁻¹)^w₁ = (a^w₁)⁻¹; invert the resulting bound using one_div_le_one_div_of_le.
keyInsights: Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted gives wGM ≤ wAM directly — Mathlib already contains this key infrastructure
(w₁a+w₂b)² ≤ w₁a²+w₂b² is Jensen for x² and reduces to w₁w₂(a-b)² ≥ 0 — a purely algebraic fact
wHM ≤ wGM follows from wGM ≤ wAM applied to reciprocals: (a⁻¹)^w₁·(b⁻¹)^w₂ = (a^w₁·b^w₂)⁻¹ ≤ w₁/a+w₂/b; inverting yields the bound
Equal weights w₁ = w₂ = 1/2 recover the standard HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM chain proved in the parent entry

sections.title: Weighted Mean Definitions
sections.summary: Defines wHM, wGM, wAM, wQM for weights w₁, w₂ and positive reals a, b.
sections.mathContext: The four weighted means: $\text{wHM} = \frac{1}{w_1/a+w_2/b}$, $\text{wGM} = a^{w_1}b^{w_2}$, $\text{wAM} = w_1 a + w_2 b$, $\text{wQM} = \sqrt{w_1 a^2 + w_2 b^2}$.

sections.title: Weighted AM-GM: wGM ≤ wAM
sections.mathContext: For $w_1+w_2=1$ and $a,b \geq 0$: $a^{w_1}b^{w_2} \leq w_1 a + w_2 b$. This is the classical weighted AM-GM, a special case of Jensen's inequality for the concave function $\log$.

sections.title: Jensen for x²: wAM ≤ wQM
sections.summary: wAM_le_wQM: squares both sides and reduces to w₁w₂(a-b)² ≥ 0 via nlinarith.
sections.mathContext: $(w_1 a + w_2 b)^2 \leq w_1 a^2 + w_2 b^2$ follows from expanding and using $w_1+w_2=1$: the difference is $w_1 w_2(a-b)^2 \geq 0$.

sections.title: Reciprocal Argument: wHM ≤ wGM
sections.summary: wHM_le_wGM: applies wGM ≤ wAM to a⁻¹ and b⁻¹, uses Real.inv_rpow, inverts.
sections.mathContext: Apply weighted AM-GM to $1/a$, $1/b$: $(1/a)^{w_1}(1/b)^{w_2} \leq w_1/a+w_2/b$. Since $(1/a)^{w_1} = (a^{w_1})^{-1}$, LHS $= (a^{w_1}b^{w_2})^{-1}$. Inverting both sides (both positive) gives $1/(w_1/a+w_2/b) \leq a^{w_1}b^{w_2}$.

sections.title: Full Weighted Mean Chain
sections.summary: weighted_mean_chain: wHM ≤ wGM ≤ wAM ≤ wQM. Plus equal-weight specialization and diagonal equality.
sections.mathContext: The full chain for general weights. Equal weights ($w_1=w_2=1/2$) recover $\text{HM} \leq \text{GM} \leq \text{AM} \leq \text{QM}$. All means coincide when $a=b$.

conclusion.summary: Mathlib has full infrastructure for the weighted power mean chain. The key lemma Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted plus Real.inv_rpow and elementary algebra complete the proof in 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The weighted chain generalizes the equal-weight result and covers asymmetric distributions. For the quantum context: the equal-weight case gives the Robertson-Schrödinger bound; the weighted version covers mixed quantum states with arbitrary occupation probabilities.
openQuestions: Can the n-variable weighted power mean chain M_{p₁}^w ≤ M_{p₂}^w for p₁ ≤ p₂ be formalized using Finset sums and Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean_weighted?
Does the equality condition wAM = wQM iff a = b have a clean Lean proof using Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff?
